claim_summary: OntoAR-HAR contributes a training-free, feedback-driven HAR classifier that follows a confusion-guided activity hierarchy, grounds child choices in population and gated user-memory examples, and uses offline-refined executable sensor features.

claim_evidence.quote: We propose OntoAR-HAR, an ontology-guided agentic RAG framework for HAR that combines a static population knowledge store with a personalized knowledge store.
ontology represents inclusion and sibling relations among activity labels and turns one global retrieval problem into a sequence of local decisions.
At each ambiguous node, an LLM proposes a structured list of feature names, physical interpretations, and calculations from the child labels and sensor metadata.

After prediction, a prompt-based gate decides whether (xq , ŷ) enters Dp . The gate checks agreement between static population retrieval, personal retrieval when available, and the node feature ranges; ambiguous or contradictory cases are not inserted.

modules.name: Ontology-guided node-constrained retrieval and traversal
modules.scope_reason: R3.1 TSK: the activity ontology, retrieval mask, and sibling choices directly define the classification output; changing task families would require redesigning the hierarchy, masks, and child-selection objective. The input windows are temporal, but the operative rule is bound to HAR labels, so R3.2 GTS is less specific.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - ontology and sibling candidate decisions define the classification output
R4:Planning and Orchestration; Memory and Context; Tools and Execution

evidence.quote: ontology represents inclusion and sibling relations among activity labels and turns one global retrieval problem into a sequence of local decisions.
For each sensor view, the static population store Dg contains source embeddings and labels. A logical mask restricts retrieval at node v to examples whose labels occur below v:

The agent moves to ĉv until reaching a leaf ŷ. This coarseto-fine path directly represents cases such as activity → locomotion → walking direction, so a feature is evaluated only where it distinguishes siblings.

modules.name: Gated personalized episodic memory
modules.scope_reason: R3.1 TSK: the memory gate admits windows as accepted activity labels and checks population and personal retrieval plus node feature ranges; a different task family would require different memory keys and admission criteria. The state uses earlier windows, but temporal availability is subordinate to this classification-specific validator, so R3.2 GTS does not decide the layer.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - the admission criterion depends on activity labels and classification evidence
R4:Memory and Context; Planning and Orchestration

evidence.quote: The personalized store Dp has the same representation but is initialized empty for each inference user. It contains previously observed query windows paired with accepted predictions.

After prediction, a prompt-based gate decides whether (xq , ŷ) enters Dp . The gate checks agreement between static population retrieval, personal retrieval when available, and the node feature ranges; ambiguous or contradictory cases are not inserted.

modules.name: LLM iterative executable feature construction
modules.scope_reason: R3.1 TSK: features are proposed for child activity labels and scored by separation of confused activity classes; changing task families would change the objective and feature set. Although the calculations operate on time-series windows (R3.2 GTS signal), the task objective is the more specific first match.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - feature proposals and scoring use activity-class distinctions
R4:Optimization and Evolution; Tools and Execution
